briefs.teaching: The evening Shema may be recited until the night is over (the Sages' midnight is a fence), as Rabban Gamliel's sons learn.
briefs.scene: Rabban Gamliel sits at a table by a lamp. His two sons burst in from a wedding feast, still in festive clothes, as the sky outside the window turns grey with the first light.
briefs.stake: Above the scene, a night arc with three marked points (first watch, midnight, dawn). A bubble over the sons shows a '?' beside a moon, answered by a sun just rising.
briefs.must_show: two young men in festive clothes; a father reading by lamplight; a window with pre-dawn sky; sense of 'late but not too late'.
briefs.avoid: Full daylight (the point is that it is not yet dawn); alcohol or drunkenness (not in the source).
briefs.overlay: Arc labels: R. Eliezer / Sages / Rabban Gamliel.

briefs.teaching: Morning Shema begins when it is light enough to tell certain colors apart; the end of the time is disputed.
briefs.scene: A man at a window at first light holds the fringes of his tzitzit up to the pale sky.
briefs.stake: Two thought bubbles: one shows a blue thread beside a white thread, the other a blue thread beside a green one, each with a '?'. A second sun/clock mark shows sunrise and the third hour.
briefs.must_show: tzitzit with a blue thread; dawn light; two comparison bubbles.
briefs.avoid: Showing which opinion is right; sunlight already high.
briefs.overlay: First opinion: blue/white. R. Eliezer: blue/green. Ends: sunrise / 3rd hour (R. Yehoshua).

briefs.teaching: Beit Shammai: recline in the evening, stand in the morning. Beit Hillel: each as he is. Rabbi Tarfon followed Beit Shammai on the road and was endangered.
briefs.scene: At night on a country road, Rabbi Tarfon lies on his side to say Shema while two figures approach through the trees.
briefs.stake: Two bubbles flank him: one with a reclining figure and a standing figure (Shammai), one with a walking figure (Hillel). A small '?' over him.
briefs.must_show: a man on the ground by a road at night; approaching strangers; the two posture bubbles.
briefs.avoid: Violence shown (the source says only 'danger'); making the approaching figures a stereotype.
briefs.overlay: Beit Shammai / Beit Hillel; evening vs. morning.

briefs.teaching: Number of blessings around Shema in the morning and evening; where a blessing is long or short, and where it ends with a blessing formula, one may not change it.
briefs.scene: Diagram: the Shema in the center, blessings before and after, with morning and evening rows.
briefs.stake: Counts shown by blocks: morning 2 before, 1 after; evening 2 before, 2 after.
briefs.avoid: Implying the names of the blessings are in the mishnah (Kulp adds them).

briefs.teaching: The Exodus is mentioned at night: Ben Zoma reads 'all the days of your life' as including nights; the Sages read it as including the days of the Messiah.
briefs.scene: A beit midrash. A young scholar (Ben Zoma) explains to an older, white-bearded sage (R. Elazar ben Azariah) while others listen.
briefs.stake: Two bubbles over the group: a sun for 'days' and a moon added by the word 'all'; a second bubble with a crown or rising sun for the Messiah.
briefs.must_show: teacher/student pair; the sun and moon bubbles.
briefs.avoid: Rabbi Elazar's age beyond what the source gives ('almost seventy').
briefs.overlay: 'the days of your life' / 'all the days of your life'.
